ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The channel transition probability table in the attached figure uses X as rows and Y as columns; the columns are Y=0, Y=1, Y=2, and the rows are X=0, X=1. In the table, the X=0 row corresponds to probabilities P(Y=0|X=0)=0.8, P(Y=1|X=0)=0, P(Y=2|X=0)=0.2; the X=1 row corresponds to probabilities P(Y=0|X=1)=0, P(Y=1|X=1)=0.8, P(Y=2|X=1)=0.2. Reasoning: Let P(X=0)=p, P(X=1)=1-p, then the output distribution is P(Y=0)=0.8p, P(Y=1)=0.8(1-p), P(Y=2)=0.2. The entropies of the two rows of conditional distributions are the same, both H_b(0.2), so H(Y|X)=H_b(0.2). The output entropy can be written as H(Y)=H_b(0.2)+0.8H_b(p), because the total probability 0.8 is allocated between Y=0 and Y=1 according to p and 1-p. Therefore the mutual information I(X;Y)=H(Y)-H(Y|X)=0.8H_b(p). The binary entropy H_b(p) takes its maximum value 1 bit at p=1/2, so the channel capacity C=max_p I(X;Y)=0.8 bit/symbol.

method.method_draft: From the image table, form the output distribution for input prior P(X=0)=p: P(Y=0)=0.8p, P(Y=1)=0.8(1-p), P(Y=2)=0.2. Compute H(Y|X); both rows have entropy H(0.8,0.2), so H(Y|X)=H_b(0.2). Compute H(Y) by viewing Y=2 as having fixed probability 0.2 and the remaining probability 0.8 split according to p: H(Y)=H_b(0.2)+0.8H_b(p). Therefore I(X;Y)=0.8H_b(p). Maximize over p; the maximum occurs at p=1/2, giving C=0.8 bits/symbol.

method.method_draft: Interpret the transition table as follows: with probability 0.8 the channel outputs a symbol that uniquely identifies the input, since Y=0 can only come from X=0 and Y=1 can only come from X=1. With probability 0.2 the channel outputs Y=2 regardless of input, so that symbol is an erasure carrying no information about X. Thus the channel is a binary erasure channel with erasure probability e=0.2. Apply C=1-e for a binary erasure channel, giving C=1-0.2=0.8 bits/symbol.
